result: The Health Resilience Score is calculated by taking 40% of the water quality index, 30% of the sanitation coverage, and 30% of the vaccination coverage. An area is labeled as a "Public Health Emergency" if the disease risk is 'High', the water quality index is below 50, and the calculated Health Resilience Score is less than 40. Otherwise, it's labeled as "Standard Health Status".

content: How should I calculate the "Health Resilience Score"? What is the exact formula and which columns should be used? Also, what are the exact criteria for labeling an area as "Health Crisis" vs "Normal Health Status"?

args.sql:
SELECT 
    eh.envhealthregistry,
    eh.envdistref,
    ROUND(CAST(eh.waterqualityindex * 0.4 + eh.sanitationcoverage * 0.3 + eh.vaccinationcoverage * 0.3 AS numeric), 2) AS health_resilience_score,
    CASE 
        WHEN eh.diseaserisk = 'High' AND eh.waterqualityindex < 50 AND (eh.waterqualityindex * 0.4 + eh.sanitationcoverage * 0.3 + eh.vaccinationcoverage * 0.3) < 40
        THEN 'Public Health Emergency'
        ELSE 'Standard Health Status'
    END AS status_label
FROM environmentandhealth eh
ORDER BY health_resilience_score;

SELECT 
    eh.envhealthregistry,
    d.distregistry AS disaster_registry_id,
    ROUND(CAST(eh.waterqualityindex * 0.4 + eh.sanitationcoverage * 0.3 + eh.vaccinationcoverage * 0.3 AS numeric), 2) AS health_resilience_score,
    CASE 
        WHEN eh.diseaserisk = 'High' AND eh.waterqualityindex < 50 AND (eh.waterqualityindex * 0.4 + eh.sanitationcoverage * 0.3 + eh.vaccinationcoverage * 0.3) < 40
        THEN 'Public Health Emergency'
        ELSE 'Standard Health Status'
    END AS status_label
FROM environmentandhealth eh
JOIN disasterevents d ON eh.envdistref = d.distregistry
WHERE d.haztype = 'Earthquake'
ORDER BY health_resilience_score;
